title: Log delivery contracts and adapter requirements for Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc for scoping customer-facing log delivery contracts and technical adapter requirements across the three priority SIEM targets: Splunk (HEC), Datadog (Logs API / TCP), and Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics/Data Collector API). Goal: align security, compliance, and engineering on required fields (RBAC v2 / audit schema), evidence automation hooks, PII/redaction rules, operational SLOs, and onboarding checklist for customers requesting SIEM export.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: production SIEM exports for audit events and evidence artifacts generated by Redwood Private/Dedicated/Hosted control plane and key product surfaces (auth, deployments, rollouts, billing events relevant to compliance).
- Export types: structured audit logs (JSON), evidence snapshot pointers (signed URLs/attachments), and periodic delivery of aggregated telemetry (usage counters) where requested.
- Not in scope: raw GPU metrics, internal-only debug traces, or third-party telemetry we do not control.

High-level requirements (customer contract minimums):
- Delivery mode: push to customer SIEM via HEC/Datadog/Log Analytics collector or customer pull endpoint (SFTP/S3) as fallbacks.
- Event retention guarantee: we will retain a copy of audit events for 90 days for export requests; customers can request longer retention under contract.
- Delivery SLA: near-real-time (best effort <30s for control plane critical events) or batched hourly deliveries for low-priority events. Specify chosen mode in contract.
- RBAC & scope: exported events must include RBAC v2 context (subject_id, subject_type, role_ids, grant_id, resource_type, resource_id) to allow customers to perform cross-checks with their own identity systems.
- Evidence automation: support a standardized evidence bundle descriptor (evidence_id, event_refs, artefact_urls, digest_sha256, signed_by). See schema below.
- PII redaction options: by default redact email and full user names for non-admin exports; customer can opt-in to unredacted exports with BizOps/legal signoff and compliance review.

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields):
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- event_id: uuid v4
- event_type: short string (auth.login, auth.failed, deployment.start, rollout.canary, api.key.create, billing.invoice.generate, siem.export.request)
- severity: INFO | WARNING | ERROR | CRITICAL
- actor: { subject_id, subject_type, display_name (nullable) }  -- include subject attributes but allow redaction per contract
- rbac_context: { grant_id, roles: [role_id,...], principal_source (okta/saml/local) }
- resource: { resource_type, resource_id, resource_name (nullable) }
- request: optional freeform object with URL/route, method, remote_ip (cidr optional)
- outcome: success | failure | partial, with error_code and error_message where applicable
- trace_ids: list of tracing ids for cross-correlation (span_id, trace_id)
- evidence_refs: list of evidence_id that link to evidence bundles (see evidence schema)
- schema_version: "audit_v2"

Note: For drive exports to SIEM that cannot carry nested objects, flatten fields using dot-notation: actor.subject_id, rbac.grant_id, resource.type, request.remote_ip, etc. Provide mapping examples per connector below.

RBAC v2 export guidance (what to include and why):
- Provide grant_id on all authz events so customers can reconcile permission changes with observed actions.
- List roles as stable ids (not display names) and include a roles_delta field on role-change events.
- On impersonation or service-account flows, include impersonator_id and impersonation_reason.
- For privacy, include subject_email only when export is to a secure, contractually approved SIEM endpoint and customer has opted-in.

Evidence automation schema (bundle descriptor):
- evidence_id: uuid
- created_at: ISO-8601
- origin_event_id: event_id that generated the evidence
- artifacts: list of objects with { name, url, sha256, size_bytes, content_type }
- access_policy: { expires_at, signed_url: true|false, allowed_ips: [] }
- signer: service_account_id or principal that signed the bundle
- verification_digest: base64(signature_over_manifest)
- retention_policy_tag: e.g., audit-90d, legal-7y
- note: if the SIEM target cannot host artifacts, we export an evidence pointer event with the manifest embedded or a minimal pointer containing evidence_id and a short url.

Connector specifics per SIEM:
1) Splunk HEC (recommended for most enterprise customers)
- Preferred payload: JSON events via HEC using batches up to 1000 events or 5MB payloads. Use event metadata fields: host (redwood-inference), source (redwood-audit), sourcetype (redwood:audit:v2). Add custom fields for rbac/grant_id and evidence_refs flattened.
- Example flattened field names: actor_subject_id, rbac_grant_id, resource_type, evidence_refs
- Auth: HEC token (TLS mandatory). Support mutual TLS for high-security customers.
- Backpressure: implement exponential backoff on 429 + jitter. Support persistent queue on disk up to contract size.
- Delivery acknowledgements: treat 2xx as success; non-2xx should trigger retry policy with alert to customer if >5 failed batches in 1h.

2) Datadog Logs API / TCP ingestion
- Preferred payload: Datadog JSON logs with tags. Include ddsource=redwood, ddtags=customer:<id>,event_type:audit. Datadog requires single-line JSON objects. Flatten nested fields.
- Rate limiting: Datadog enforces per-API-key throughput; include adaptive batching and local throttling.
- Example tags: "rbac:grant_<grant_id>", "resource:deployment_<id>" but avoid embedding PII in tags.
- If using TCP/forwarder, ensure newline-delimited JSON and proper backpressure handling.

3) Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics (Data Collector API)
- The Data Collector API accepts JSON arrays with a schema per custom log; prefer a single custom log type Redwood_Audit_CL. Each record should be flattened key:value pairs.
- Azure expects UTF-8 and HMAC-SHA256 authorization header; provide sample scripts for customers.
- For very large volumes, recommend using Event Hubs ingestion or customer-side staging in storage account.

Field mapping examples (flattened payload for all targets):
- time, event_id, event_type, severity, actor_subject_id, actor_type, rbac_grant_id, rbac_roles, resource_type, resource_id, resource_name, request_method, request_path, request_remote_ip, outcome, error_code, evidence_refs, trace_id, schema_version

PII and redaction policy (configurable per-customer):
- Default redact: email, phone, ssn-like strings, full display names. Keep subject_id (opaque GUID) for correlation.
- Allowlist approach: customer provides list of approved fields to include unredacted. Legal signoff required.
- Redaction mechanics: sanitise before export with deterministic masking where ordered (e.g., user_email -> user***@domain.com) when requested.

Operational SLOs and monitoring hooks:
- Delivery latency: median <30s for critical events; 99p <120s for push mode assuming no upstream throttling.
- Delivery success rate: 99.5% monthly for production connectors.
- Alerting: auto-create PagerDuty incident on persistent delivery failure (>15m) and on evidence-signing failure.
- Observability: emit metrics: exported_events_total, export_failures_total{reason,siem}, export_latency_seconds_bucket, evidence_signed_total.

Onboarding checklist (customer + Redwood):
- Customer to provide: HEC token / Datadog API key / Log Analytics workspace ID + key, preferred delivery mode, required retention and redaction policy, allowed IP CIDRs for signed URLs (optional), contract start date and SLAs.
- Redwood to provide: test endpoint and sample events, mapping guide, schema versioning policy, digest/signing public key, runbook for incidents, and an initial week of elevated monitoring and contact points.
- Security review: run a short threat model for the export channel (mutual TLS recommended for exports with PII), update ATO/attestation artifacts as needed.

Minimum connector acceptance criteria (ENG readiness):
- End-to-end test that sends 10k synthetic events and validates field mappings, batching, and retries under simulated 429/5xx.
- Evidence bundle flow test: generate evidence from event, sign, upload, and verify pointer appears in SIEM and resolves to signed manifest.
- RBAC v2 fields present for all authz-related events, with optional redaction toggles exercised.
- Automated integration tests in CI that run against a mocked/localhost SIEM target.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should we support event-level differential masking (mask only when subject is customer_end_user vs employee)?
- How to coordinate role id schema across product and export contract to ensure stable role IDs? (proposal: use stable, numeric role ids published to Confluence + semantic names)
- Longer retention tiers pricing and storage model for evidence artifacts beyond 90 days.

Next actions (owners):
- Aisha: draft sample HEC payloads and upload to the docs repo (SEC-4123) by 2024-04-01.
- Ben: prototype resilient sender with disk-backed queue and backoff policy; lab tests by 2024-04-15.
- Marina: define evidence bundle signing format and produce verification script for customers by 2024-04-10.
- Solutions Eng: prepare a customer onboarding checklist and template contract clause for export SLOs.

References and artifacts:
- Confluence: SIEM export guidelines (linked above)
- Jira: SEC-4123, SEC-4201 (evidence signing), ENG-TEL-789 (sender reliability)
- Example scripts: gitlab.com/redwood/telemetry-adapters (MR 88)

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep the schema stable (audit_v2) and make non-breaking additive changes only.
- For customers with very strict egress policies, we may need to offer a private connector appliance (on-prem relay) — ticketize and price separately.
- Remember to align with product team on which control-plane events are considered "evidence-critical" vs "operational" so customers can pick only the former if they want reduced volume.
